about: The surfaces the static pre-scan looks for in a migration, kept as data so the list is reviewable as a list and a diff shows exactly which target moved. Target grammar: 'Class::method' (that method on that class, static or instance), '*::method' (that method on any receiver), 'function()' (a free function), 'Class' (any call on that class), 'Namespace\*' (any call under that namespace). Within a catalog the first matching entry wins, so a specific target may sit in front of a broad one.

indirect_call_exempt.description: Classes an indirect-call hit is deliberately NOT raised for. The indirect-call detector flags a migration that reaches project code the pre-scan cannot follow — but the whole framework, and a handful of pure value surfaces, are neither project code nor side effects, and flagging them would make the rule noise. An application adds its own exemptions through sqlens.capture.prescan.indirect_calls.allowlist rather than editing this list.

introspection_guards.description: Schema-introspection calls whose answer steers a migration's control flow — the classic if (Schema::hasTable(...)) { ... } guard. Measured against the framework: under pretend these return their EMPTY answer (hasTable is false for a table that really exists) AND the introspection SELECT is itself logged. So the guarded block never runs, its DDL is never captured, and the statement list is non-empty yet holds none of the real work. A capture that trusted either half would report a clean pass over DDL it never saw.

side_effects.description: Surfaces that reach the world outside the database. Pretend mode intercepts SQL and nothing else: the PHP around it runs for real, so a notification in a migration is sent, an HTTP call is made, a file is written, a job is queued — from a command whose whole purpose is to look at a migration without running it. A lint run that sends a message to a customer is the worst thing this tool could do, so a migration touching any of these is never captured, and is reported before anything of it executes.

result_dependent.description: Calls whose result decides what SQL a migration emits. Pretend mode answers every query with an empty result set, so a loop over one runs zero times and a branch on one is never taken: the captured SQL would be a strict subset of the real SQL, and the run would be green for the wrong reason.

result_dependent_exempt.description: Surfaces that carry a method name from the result-dependent catalog without reading the database. Method names alone cannot separate 'Config::get' from a query builder's 'get', because the receiver's type is not statically known — so the exceptions are written down here, each with its reason, rather than hidden in the detector. This catalog is consulted first: a call it covers is never a result-dependent hit.
